title: Cambridge Dictionary names ‘human’ its word of the year as AI spreads
excerpt: Cambridge Dictionary named 'human' its 2026 word of the year, saying AI has changed how the word is used, from human-made to human-written.
content_html:
Cambridge Dictionary has named human its word of the year for 2026. It said the rise of AI has given the word new weight, the Guardian reported.

The dictionary defines human as “having the qualities, faults and feelings that people have, as opposed to gods, animals or machines.”

“AI is changing how we talk about being human,” said Colin McIntosh, an editor at Cambridge Dictionary.

McIntosh pointed to the growing use of terms such as human-made, which people use to set their work apart from AI output. He said worries about outsourcing our thinking had made people rethink how much they rely on AI.

Other words on the shortlist included agent, now used for AI systems that carry out tasks without a person in control. Wholesome also made the list, as did a word tied to non-digital activities, the Guardian reported.

Last year, Cambridge chose parasocial, partly because of the one-sided bonds people form with AI chatbots. Earlier this month, Collins picked mogging, meaning to outshine someone.

New additions to the dictionary this year include looksmaxxing and aura farming, according to the Guardian.
